title: Forward-deployed engineers are the AI industry’s latest talent obsession
author: Modelverse Editorial
excerpt: A new study estimates only 2,000 U.S. engineers have the expertise to deliver meaningful AI ROI, as enterprises race to hire forward-deployed engineers to implement AI at scale.
body:
## Introduction to Forward-Deployed Engineers
The AI industry is witnessing a significant shift in talent acquisition, with forward-deployed engineers (FDEs) emerging as the most sought-after specialists. According to a recent study, there are only approximately 2,000 engineers in the US who possess the unique combination of sector expertise, gravitas, and hands-on AI experience required to drive returns on AI investments.

## The Rise of FDEs
As enterprises transition from accessing AI models to implementing them in workflows, the demand for FDEs is skyrocketing. These engineers work within client organizations to build, implement, and deploy software or AI models, making them crucial for meaningful bottom-line improvements. The study projects a staggering 2,100% surge in demand for FDEs by the end of the year, with 70% of companies already planning to hire them.

## Implications for Developers and Researchers
The rapid growth in demand for FDEs will outstrip supply, with only approximately 17,000 US-based FDEs available, many of whom are already employed. This talent obsession has significant implications for developers and researchers, as companies scramble to acquire the necessary expertise to drive AI implementation and deployment. The study's findings highlight the need for professionals to develop the skills required to become FDEs, making them highly sought after in the industry.
